Exercise 15.7.18 — Evaluate the Triple Integral

Problem. Evaluate the triple integral ∭Ez dV, \iiint_E z\, dV, ∭E​zdV, where EEE is bounded by the cylinder y2+z2=9y^2 + z^2 = 9y2+z2=9 and the planes x=0x = 0x=0, y=3xy = 3xy=3x, and z=0z = 0z=0 in the first octant.

Notation used in this solution

SymbolMeaning
dVdVdV Volume element. In the order we use, dV=dx dz dydV = dx\,dz\,dydV=dxdzdy is the small box of volume spanned by the differentials dxdxdx, dzdzdz, dydydy.
∭E\iiint_E∭E​ Triple integral over the solid region EEE. The three integrations run through the three spatial directions once each.
y=3xy = 3xy=3x A vertical plane through the zzz-axis. Solving for xxx gives x=y/3x = y/3x=y/3, the upper xxx-limit of the solid.
DDD The projection of EEE onto the yzyzyz-plane: the quarter disk y2+z2≤9y^2 + z^2 \leq 9y2+z2≤9 with y≥0y \geq 0y≥0, z≥0z \geq 0z≥0.
rrr, θ\thetaθ Polar coordinates in the yzyzyz-plane: y=rcos⁡θy = r\cos\thetay=rcosθ, z=rsin⁡θz = r\sin\thetaz=rsinθ, so dy dz=r dr dθdy\,dz = r\,dr\,d\thetadydz=rdrdθ. Used for the independent check.

Part 1 — Set up and evaluate

Step 1.1: Describe the solid.

In the first octant we have x≥0x \geq 0x≥0, y≥0y \geq 0y≥0, z≥0z \geq 0z≥0. The cylinder y2+z2=9y^2 + z^2 = 9y2+z2=9 has its axis along the xxx-direction and radius 333. Its projection onto the yzyzyz-plane is the quarter disk D={(y,z):0≤y≤3,  0≤z≤9−y2}D = \{(y,z) : 0 \leq y \leq 3,\; 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{9 - y^2}\}D={(y,z):0≤y≤3,0≤z≤9−y2​}. The plane x=0x = 0x=0 is the back wall; the plane y=3xy = 3xy=3x, i.e. x=y/3x = y/3x=y/3, is the front slant wall; and z=0z = 0z=0 is the floor.

So for each (y,z)∈D(y,z) \in D(y,z)∈D the vertical line in the xxx-direction runs from x=0x = 0x=0 to x=y/3x = y/3x=y/3: E={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,  0≤x≤y3}. E = \left\{ (x,y,z) : (y,z) \in D,\; 0 \leq x \leq \tfrac{y}{3} \right\}. E={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,0≤x≤3y​}.

Step 1.2: Choose the order of integration.

Integrate in xxx first (the short, straight range), then over the quarter disk DDD:

∭Ez dV=∫03∫09−y2∫0y/3z  dx dz dy. \iiint_E z\,dV = \int_0^3 \int_0^{\sqrt{9-y^2}} \int_0^{y/3} z\; dx\, dz\, dy. ∭E​zdV=∫03​∫09−y2​​∫0y/3​zdxdzdy.

Step 1.3: Evaluate the inner integral.

∫0y/3z dx=z ∣0y/3=y z3. \int_0^{y/3} z\,dx = z\,\bigg|_0^{y/3} = \frac{y\,z}{3}. ∫0y/3​zdx=z​0y/3​=3yz​.

Since the integrand is independent of xxx, the length of the xxx-range, y/3y/3y/3, multiplies zzz.

Step 1.4: Integrate over zzz.

∫09−y2yz3 dz=y3⋅z22∣09−y2=y6 (9−y2). \int_0^{\sqrt{9-y^2}} \frac{y z}{3}\,dz = \frac{y}{3}\cdot\frac{z^2}{2}\bigg|_0^{\sqrt{9-y^2}} = \frac{y}{6}\,(9 - y^2). ∫09−y2​​3yz​dz=3y​⋅2z2​​09−y2​​=6y​(9−y2).

Step 1.5: Integrate over yyy.

∫03y(9−y2)6 dy=16[9y22−y44]03=16(812−814)=16⋅814=278. \int_0^3 \frac{y(9-y^2)}{6}\,dy = \frac{1}{6}\left[\frac{9y^2}{2} - \frac{y^4}{4}\right]_0^3 = \frac{1}{6}\left(\frac{81}{2} - \frac{81}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{6}\cdot\frac{81}{4} = \frac{27}{8}. ∫03​6y(9−y2)​dy=61​[29y2​−4y4​]03​=61​(281​−481​)=61​⋅481​=827​.

Step 1.6: Independent check in polar coordinates.

Write y=rcos⁡θy = r\cos\thetay=rcosθ, z=rsin⁡θz = r\sin\thetaz=rsinθ in DDD (0≤r≤3,  0≤θ≤π/2)(0 \leq r \leq 3,\; 0 \leq \theta \leq \pi/2)(0≤r≤3,0≤θ≤π/2). Then xxx runs from 000 to rcos⁡θ3\frac{r\cos\theta}{3}3rcosθ​ and the integral becomes

∫0π/2∫03(rcos⁡θ3)(rsin⁡θ)  r dr dθ=13∫0π/2cos⁡θsin⁡θ dθ⏟= 1/2∫03r3 dr⏟= 81/4=13⋅12⋅814=278, \int_0^{\pi/2}\int_0^3 \left(\frac{r\cos\theta}{3}\right) \big(r\sin\theta\big)\; r\,dr\,d\theta = \frac{1}{3}\underbrace{\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos\theta\sin\theta\,d\theta}_{=\,1/2} \underbrace{\int_0^3 r^3\,dr}_{=\,81/4} = \frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{81}{4} = \frac{27}{8}, ∫0π/2​∫03​(3rcosθ​)(rsinθ)rdrdθ=31​=1/2∫0π/2​cosθsinθdθ​​=81/4∫03​r3dr​​=31​⋅21​⋅481​=827​,

Remark. The factor ∫0π/2cos⁡θ sin⁡θ dθ=1/2\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos\theta\,\sin\theta\,d\theta = 1/2∫0π/2​cosθsinθdθ=1/2 comes from ∫sin⁡θ dθ=−cos⁡θ\int \sin\theta\,d\theta = -\cos\theta∫sinθdθ=−cosθ; the factor 81/481/481/4 is the standard r4/4r^4/4r4/4 antiderivative. Both agree with the rectangular computation above.

Result. ∭Ez dV=278=3.375. \iiint_E z\, dV = \frac{27}{8} = 3.375. ∭E​zdV=827​=3.375.

Step 1.7: Verification by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py evaluates the same integral twice with SymPy: once as the iterated integral ∫03 ⁣∫09−y2 ⁣∫0y/3z dx dz dy\int_0^3 \!\int_0^{\sqrt{9-y^2}} \!\int_0^{y/3} z\,dx\,dz\,dy∫03​∫09−y2​​∫0y/3​zdxdzdy and once as the full polar iterated integral. Both calls return the exact value 27/827/827/8, confirming the hand derivation above. The figure scripts part1_figure1.py and part1_figure2.py produce the two figures embedded above.
